Despite the deceleration in earnings growth [E43], the long-term resilience of the share price, which has grown by 9% over ten years and 13% over five years, demonstrates a persistent investor interest in the stock [E11, E12].

This collapse is compounded by a Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) of -62.5%, indicating that the firm is destroying value rather than generating it [E5]. Profitability metrics are consistently negative, with compounded profit growth over the last three years at -17% and a further decline of -33% over the trailing twelve months [E9, E10]. The company’s financial instability is further highlighted by a negative book value of ₹ -0.44, rendering traditional valuation metrics like price-to-book essentially meaningless [E1].
